articles.title: Guatemala declares state of emergency in east over drug violence
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The 30-day decree covers Zacapa and Izabal, a week after Congressman Julio Portillo and three police officers were killed in an armed attack

Guatemalan authorities declared a state of emergency on Saturday (November 14, 2026) in an area battered by violence linked to drug-trafficking groups, a week after a lawmaker was killed in an attack.
The decree, effective from Saturday for 30 days, restricts outdoor gatherings and bolsters powers for security forces in the eastern departments of Zacapa and Izabal.

Under the decree, security forces will be able to disperse groups by force, make arrests and enter residences without a warrant. The government said in a statement that the purpose of the decree was to “strengthen security” and “protect the population.”

Last week, Congressman Julio Portillo and three police officers were killed in an armed attack targeting the lawmaker in the town of Rio Hondo in Zacapa. The Lorenzana family cartel, which has ties to Mexico’s Sinaloa cartel, controls the drug trade in Zacapa.
The Lorenzanas were designated a terrorist organisation by the United States on Friday (November 13, 2026), along with the Mendoza family cartel, which has a strong presence in Izabal.

articles.title: Keralam government to hold talks with LPST protesters
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister’s Office informs protesters that the government is willing for talks as the agitation led by the All Kerala Lower Primary School Teachers (LPST) Rankholders’ Association enters its 133rd day

The Keralam government will hold talks with the representatives of the All Kerala Lower Primary School Teachers (LPST) Rankholders’ Association who have been on an agitation in front of the Secretariat for the past 133 days. The Chief Minister’s Office on Sunday informed the protesters that the government is willing for talks.
S. Valarmathi, the association secretary, who is on a fast-unto-death protest, said the agitation will be withdrawn only if the government agrees to the demands.

The LPST rank-holders began their protest over the delay in appointing candidates from the Kerala Public Service Commission (PSC) rank list to lower primary school teacher (LPST) posts, along with demands for changes to the teacher-recruitment system and teacher-student ratio.
The agitation, which began as a demand for appointment orders, has now expanded into a broader dispute over how teaching vacancies are calculated, reported and filled.

The LPST rank list came into effect in all 14 districts on May 31, 2025. The list reportedly has around 11,758 candidates, but fewer than 500 appointments had been made by August, according to reports.

articles.title: Lalit Modi announces he has acquired British citizenship
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Lalit Modi announced on X that he had been naturalised as a British citizen on September 20; says United Kingdom has been my home for many years

Indian Premier League (IPL) founder Lalit Modi, who has had a number of cases and investigations against him in India, announced over the weekend that he had become a British citizen. The loss of Indian citizenship – which is automatic when one accepts the citizenship of another country – further complicates the process of extraditing Mr. Modi to India.
Mr. Modi announced on X that he had been naturalised as a British citizen on September 20.

New Delhi has repeatedly pressed the U.K. for the return of Mr. Modi, along with others such as diamond jeweller Nirav Modi and entrepreneur Vija Mallya, to India to face legal proceedings. Prime Minister Narendra Modi made requests to his (then) British counterpart Keir Starmer for the return of “economic offenders and fugitives” in July 2025, when he visited the U.K., according to a government readout of their meeting.
Mr. Lalit Modi announced his new citizenship status in person at the Oxford Union on Saturday (November 14, 2026), he said, noting that November 14 was also the birthday of King Charles III.
“Thank you to my family, friends and everyone who has been part of this journey, and to the Oxford Union for providing such a memorable occasion to share this news,” he said.
“The United Kingdom has been my home for many years,” he said.

He was accused in India of financial irregularities and money laundering, as well as violating the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), stemming from his time as the Vice President of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) during the 2009-2010 period. A case against Mr. Lalit Modi under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, based on an FIR filed by the Tamil Nadu police on October 13, 2010.
A non-bailable warrant was issued against Mr. Lalit Modi in 2015 after he failed to respond to multiple summonses from the Enforcement Directorate (ED).

🇬🇧 A PROUD MOMENT. A NEW CHAPTER. Today, 14 November 2026, I had the honour of addressing the Oxford Union, where I publicly shared a very special and personal milestone. I AM PROUD TO BE A BRITISH CITIZEN. 🇬🇧 On 15 September 2026, surrounded by family and friends, I celebrated my British citizenship at a ceremony that will always hold a special place in my heart. The United Kingdom has been my home for many years. It is a country I have come to admire and appreciate deeply — its people, institutions, traditions and values. Becoming British is a privilege and a responsibility that I embrace with pride, gratitude and a genuine sense of belonging. My life's journey has been shaped by different cultures and experiences, and I look forward to continuing to contribute positively to the country I proudly call home. Thank you to my family, friends and everyone who has been part of this journey, and to the Oxford Union for providing such a memorable occasion to share this news. A new chapter, with much to look forward to. And on His Majesty King Charles III's birthday, a particularly special day to share this moment. God Save the King! 🇬🇧👑 Lalit Modi Founder IPL #BritishCitizen #OxfordUnion #UnitedKingdom #GodSaveTheKing

On February 6, 2017, the ED requested the U.K. authorities to transfer Mr. Lalit Modi to India to face justice in relation to the non-bailable warrant. It used the Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty (MLAT) process for this.

In 2025, the Ministry of External Affairs said it would continue to pursue the case against Mr. Lalit Modi as per the law, reacting to the news that Mr. Lalit Modi had surrendered his Indian passport to the Indian High Commission in London following his acquisition of citizenship of Vanuatu. (The Prime Minister of Vanuatu, Jothan Napat, subsequently ordered the cancellation of Mr. Lalit Modi’s passport and a probe into his citizenship).

Mr. Lalit Modi was also involved in a case relating to the shifting of the IPL tournament from India to South Africa in 2009. This happened due to security concerns around the general election and necessitated the transfer of funds from BCCI to Cricket South Africa. This process, the ED alleged, had involved violations of FEMA. Consequently, the ED imposed penalties on Mr. Lalit Modi in 2018. In July 2026, Mr. Lalit Modi had a legal victory when an appellate tribunal overturned the findings against him and set aside the penalties.

articles.title: All sugar factories cannot pay same price to farmers, says Satish Jarkiholi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Union government should revise Minimum Selling Price of sugar, according to the Minister

“All factories cannot pay same price to sugarcane farmers. Sugarcane procurement prices depend on various factors like the quality of the crop, sugar recovery percentage, prevailing market price of sugar and the financial condition of the sugar factory,” Minister Satish Jarkiholi, who is also a sugar factory owner, said in Belagavi on Saturday.
He told reporters that the demand for uniform pricing for sugarcane across the State is natural and understandable.

“But, it is impractical. A factory with better financial health can usually pay higher prices to farmers compared to a factory that is suffering losses or is under a huge debt burden. Climatic factors also contribute. Farmers should understand that prices can differ from factory to factory and district to district,” he said.

“Our objective is to ensure that sugarcane growers receive a fair price. We have no objection if sugar factories that possess the financial capacity to pay a higher rate choose to do so. However, the financial condition of all sugar factories is not the same,” he said.
“Factories are offering varying rates not only in Belagavi district but also in Kalaburagi and Haveri districts. But that is a natural phenomenon, especially in a drought year,” he said.

“Factories that are in a position to pay a higher rate should do so. We have no opposition to this. We held several rounds of meetings with farmers and factory owners to arrive at the base price of ₹3,600 per tonne and the profit-sharing formula. This ensures additional payments to farmers if sugar prices rise. Based on this, the factories have now announced their respective rates. However, some factories are offering prices higher than this, as they want to compete with others and ensure optimum stocks,” he said.

“The yields are low this year, due to the dry spell. In Maharashtra, there has long been a practice of offering higher prices than in Karnataka. Factories there have consistently paid farmers better rates. Some farmers are comparing the prices offered by factories in Karnataka against those in Maharashtra,” he said.

“The main issue plaguing the sugar industry is the low price of sugar in the market. This is crippling the finances of the factories which are unable to pay better prices to sugarcane growers. Things will improve if the Centre hikes Minimum Selling Price of sugar. The Union government has formed a committee to examine the demand for a hike in Minimum Selling Price. The committee needs to review the farmers demands and take an appropriate decision. The crucial point is that the Union government should take the final decision. It is crucial,” he said.

articles.title: 36 arrested as excise teams uncover online supply of fermentation agent for illicit liquor
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Thirty-six people were arrested and 64 cases registered during a two-day crackdown on illicit liquor production across 42 villages in Mahabubabad and Tandur mandals, where producers sourced a fermentation agent online after the supply of jaggery and sugar was restricted.

Excise officials found that people in tribal hamlets had switched to a sugar-like substance used in baking cakes to prepare the fermentation mixture. The raids, conducted by 17 teams, resulted in the seizure of 217 litres of illicit liquor. Officials destroyed 9,450 litres of fermentation mixture. They also seized 565 kgs of jaggery, 25 kgs of a fermentation ingredient, and six vehicles. Another 40 people were bound over.

The drive was launched by Excise Enforcement Director Avinash Mohanty and covered 42 villages over two days. The operation was supervised by Excise Enforcement Joint Commissioner Anjan Rao, Warangal District Deputy Commissioner Dattu Raj Goud, Assistant Commissioner K. Naveen Kumar and ES Karan Chand.

articles.title: What is Megaspeed International, the firm under scanner over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang affair
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Megaspeed International has come under the scanner after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with Alice Huang, a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.

Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing firm, is in the spotlight after the alleged extramarital affair of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang with one of the company’s former executives, Alice Huang. Ms Huang is accused of being a Chinese spy.
On November 15, 2026, Megaspeed said that Alice Huang had officially left Megaspeed on August 30, 2025 and had no current role at the company.
“Megaspeed does not ​comment on ‌Ms. Huang’s personal and private matters,” the company added in ‌a statement.
“Megaspeed is ​aware of recent media reports ⁠containing assertions about our business, supply chain ‌and global operations that are not supported by verifiable evidence.”
The company said it conducted “legitimate ‌and lawful business” and ​had retained external legal counsel to ⁠conduct a thorough internal ⁠investigation.

According to its website , Megaspeed is an Nvidia cloud partner in the Asia-Pacific region and a core business partner of Nvidia’s computing power cloud business. It adds that “we provide privatized, customized computing power product services covering NVIDIA’s entire GPU product line.”

A Reuters report says that Megaspeed International was incorporated in 2015 as 7Road International before changing its name to Megaspeed International in March 2023. It adds that the company is wholly owned by Singapore-registered Swiftdata, incorporated in October 2023, which says providing hosting services by non-data centers is its principal activity.

Reuters adds that Megaspeed’s assets increased sharply to $3 billion in 2024 from $33 million in 2023, its business filings showed. It reported an after-tax loss of $20 million ‌in ⁠2024, versus a loss of $21,283 a year earlier, while revenue jumped to $294 million from zero. Its cash flow statement showed $844,555 went to investing activities in 2024, after financing activities brought in cash of $10 million the previous year.

According to the company’s LinkedIn , it has around 2-10 employees and 23 associated members. The interactive map by LinkedIn shows that Megaspeed has offices in Iskandar Puteri, Malaysia; Senayan City, Indonesia; and is headquartered in the Central Region of Singapore.

Washington has restricted the export of Nvidia’s most cutting-edge silicon chips to China, citing national security concerns. The move is also seen as a measure to stay ahead in the field of artificial intelligence.
The New York Times has reported that the U.S. government has been probing Megaspeed since 2024 over its potential steering of Nvidia chips to China.
All of this, combined with the allegations of Ms Huang being a Chinese spy, has triggered speculation over Megaspeed’s involvement in the alleged chip transfer to China.

articles.title: Binance hack reveals crypto's uphill battle against hackers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Cryptocurrency exchanges present unusually attractive targets because hackers can identify wallets holding enormous sums of readily transferable digital assets ⁠and, in some cases, the employees with access

An elite North Korean hacking group’s $6.3 billion theft from Binance is renewing scrutiny of a longstanding weakness in the cryptocurrency industry: hackers may need to ‌compromise only one employee to get inside, while inconsistent security practices can allow them to turn that foothold ​into a massive theft.

The October 29 heist, described by experts as the largest cryptocurrency theft ever, unfolded in ⁠a matter of minutes after months of planning and preparation, according to Binance’s initial investigation.

Cybersecurity experts said the attack raises questions not only about how exchanges defend employees against sophisticated social engineering, but also about whether they have adequate internal controls to limit what an attacker can do once an employee’s computer or ‌credentials are compromised.

Social engineering is a well-understood threat in the industry, said Jonathan Alexander, chief technology officer of S&P Global’s OpenZeppelin, a blockchain security provider. The bigger question, he said, is why exchanges do not have stronger internal safeguards ‌and circuit breakers to prevent an attacker who breaches an engineer’s computer — like what happened at Binance — from escalating access and ‌moving ⁠assets.

Varying cybersecurity practices across the industry compound the problem, Alexander said, along with a longstanding aversion among some cryptocurrency advocates ⁠to controls they view as inconsistent with blockchain’s decentralized ethos that sometimes views things such as limits on transaction amounts and automatic reviews of patterns of spending as infringing on inherent privacy rights.

“I think that falsely, that has led some people to think that things like circuit breakers, things like more controls on the accounts, would be ​unacceptable or would be absolutely in conflict with that ‌need to avoid censorship,” Alexander said. “In my view, you can have security controls and have protections against that.”

The Binance attack is the latest in a string of major cryptocurrency hacks that have resulted in more than $22.3 billion in stolen funds since 2021, according to blockchain intelligence firm Chainalysis. The scale of the losses has intensified debate over whether exchanges need more consistent standards governing access, ‌transaction controls and other defenses.

“I do expect we’ll see more clarity and standardization in the kind of cybersecurity expectations and, hopefully, requirements ​for investor protection and trust,” Alexander said. “These things show why it has to change.”

Cryptocurrency exchanges present unusually attractive targets because hackers can identify wallets holding enormous sums of readily transferable digital assets ⁠and, in some cases, the employees with access to the systems controlling them.
That has made engineers and IT workers prime targets for elaborate social-engineering operations.
Alex Pruden, CEO of blockchain and digital-asset security firm Project Eleven, said defenders face a fundamental disadvantage against attackers who need to succeed ‌only once.

“This is an extremely hard problem,” Pruden said. “The best practices in cybersecurity that we’ve had up to this point are just simply not up to the task of the world that we live in in terms of what the threat is.”

fullParagraphs: The number of affected services came with significant consequences for professional users as well as entire sectors

Website status-checking tool DownDetector reported that over a lakh users had registered complaints about the Outlook email service in the outage’s early hours. articles.title: Ai+ Smartphone to increase smartphone prices by up to ₹3,000
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The smartphone prices are expected to rise up again by up to 10% post Diwali due to memory crisis, lesser inventories and rupee depreciation against US dollar
Ai+ Smartphone on Friday announced to increase the price of its smartphone portfolio by up to ₹3,000 . The new prices will be effective November 11.
The smartphone prices are expected to rise up again by up to 10% post Diwali due to memory crisis, lesser inventories and rupee depreciation against US dollar.
“With fresh inventory being procured at higher memory and component costs, the company has advanced its planned price revision to reflect the updated cost structure,” the company said.

Ai+ Smartphone, a new homegrown smartphone brand, sold over ten lakh devices during the Q3, 2026. “The decision follows stronger-than-anticipated consumer demand, with sales exceeding initial projections and existing inventory being exhausted ahead of schedule,” it added.
Recently, another Indian smartphone brand, Lava, said to increase its smartphone prices by up to ₹3,000 post Diwali.
Overall, Indian smartphone shipments went down to a decade low by 20% during the third quarter due diminishing demand and rising average smartphone price (ASP) of the phones.

articles.title: Oppo Pad Mini Review | A refreshing take on what a tablet can be
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: At a time when most tablets are getting bigger, the Pad Mini takes a different route. It is compact, remarkably light and designed for people who want a tablet they can comfortably carry around

Oppo has launched the Pad Mini in India at ₹94,999. And that is quite a price to ask for a tablet in the Indian market. However, what makes this tablet interesting is not just its hardware or premium positioning. It is the approach Oppo has taken towards its design. At a time when most tablets are getting bigger , the Pad Mini takes a different route. It is compact, remarkably light and designed for people who want a tablet they can comfortably carry around. I genuinely like this approach because portability often takes a back seat in the tablet segment. The Pad Mini also brings a matte AMOLED display, a Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 processor and an 8,000mAh battery. But can a compact tablet justify a price of ₹94,999? Let’s find out.

The first thing you notice about the Oppo Pad Mini is its size. Measuring 19.44cm in height, 13.24cm in width and just 0.55cm in thickness, the tablet feels very different from conventional tablets. It weighs approximately 279g, which makes it particularly easy to carry. You can hold it comfortably for longer periods without feeling the weight that usually comes with larger tablets. This is where Oppo’s decision to go compact makes a lot of sense.

The Lavender Purple finish adds to its appeal. It looks subtle rather than flashy and gives the tablet a distinctive identity. The flat edges keep the design clean, while the slim profile makes it feel well put together. The rear camera module sits in one corner and creates a slight protrusion. This means the tablet may wobble a little when placed on a flat surface. It is a minor design compromise, but worth mentioning.

The button placement takes some getting used to. Oppo has placed the power button and volume rocker along the top edge. The USB Type-C port sits along the bottom edge, although its slightly off-centre placement may bother those who prefer symmetrical designs. The tablet also supports face unlock, but there is no fingerprint scanner.

The Oppo Pad Mini features an 8.8-inch AMOLED display with a 2.5K resolution of 2520 × 1680 pixels. It supports an adaptive refresh rate of up to 144Hz and offers a pixel density of 344 PPI. The panel also supports 10-bit colour depth and covers 100% of the DCI-P3 colour gamut.

However, the matte finish is what makes the experience more interesting. Most tablets feature glossy displays that reflect light, particularly when you use them near windows or under bright indoor lighting. The matte treatment helps reduce reflections and makes the screen more comfortable to view under harsh lights. It also gives the display a different character when compared with conventional glossy panels.

The tab offers typical brightness of 800 nits and high-brightness mode output of up to 1,600 nits. This helps with visibility in brighter environments. The adaptive refresh rate can also scale between 60Hz and 144Hz, depending on the content. Together, these features make the Pad Mini’s display one of its strongest selling points. It is a thoughtful combination of size, resolution and screen treatment.

Under the hood, the Oppo Pad Mini runs on Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 mobile platform. It pairs the processor with 8GB of LPDDR5X RAM and 256GB of UFS 4.1 storage. This is flagship-grade hardware, and it gives the tablet enough headroom for demanding applications and everyday multi-tasking. The Adreno 829 GPU also handles the graphics workload.

The compact form factor does not mean Oppo has compromised on the core hardware. The Snapdragon platform should make the tablet suitable for productivity tasks, content consumption and gaming. The 144Hz display also complements the performance package by offering smoother scrolling and animations.

On the software front, the Pad Mini runs ColorOS 16. The interface gives the tablet its own identity and is designed to work alongside the larger display. Features such as face unlock and the tablet’s connectivity options add to the everyday experience.

The Oppo Pad Mini also gets support for the Oppo Pencil 3 Pro, which makes the compact form factor more useful beyond entertainment. Whether you want to take handwritten notes, annotate documents or sketch, stylus support adds another dimension to the tablet. The positioning of the stylus charging slot along the right edge also keeps the accessory integrated into the design.

Tablet cameras rarely decide on a purchase, and the Oppo Pad Mini does not appear to position itself as a camera-focused device. It features a 13MP rear camera with autofocus support and an 8MP front camera. The rear camera supports 4K video recording at 30fps, while the front camera records at up to 1080p at 30fps.

articles.title: ‘My entire life has been a struggle,’ says Bilkis Bano at GIO conference in Kochi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Her husband, Patel Yakub Rasool, who attended the conference, recollected the long and arduous struggle for justice she had to wage.

“My entire life has been a struggle,” Bilkis Bano, the Gujarat riots survivor who has emerged as an icon of resilience with her prolonged legal battle for justice, said in Kochi on Sunday (November 15).
Ms. Bano made the compelling remark as she inaugurated the International Conference on Women organised by the State committee of the Girls Islamic Organisation (GIO) in the city.

“Everyone knows my life story, don’t they? There is no need to say anything more about it,” she said in a brief address. Ms. Bano was gang-raped and lost seven members of her family, including her three-year-old daughter, in the 2002 riots.
Thanking those who invited her, she said, “May we continue to live with such love and peace every day, staying together all our lives.”

Her husband, Patel Yakub Rasool, who attended the conference, recollected the long and arduous struggle for justice she had to wage. “The family had to relocate several times, and her rights were denied. They had to repeatedly bring instances of injustice to the attention of those in positions of power. What happened to Bilkis is now known to the entire world. May her struggle inspire every woman to find the strength to raise her voice for her rights,” he said.
The conference was presided over by GIO State president K. Shifana. Jamia Millia Islamia student leader Nousheen Farooq was the chief guest.

Saria Cheruvallil, Professor at Coventry University, UK; Dalia Saleh, researcher at the University of Cambridge; Reem Mahmoud Al Haddad, Palestinian writer and journalist; Jamaat-e-Islami national secretary A. Rahmathunnisa; and Jamaat-e-Islami Keralam ameer P. Mujeeb Rahman were among those who spoke at various sessions.

articles.title: P. Viswanathan and Selvaperunthagai spar over comments on T.N.’s law and order situation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Minister questions the former TNCC president on which party he is going to next
Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan. | Photo Credit: B. VELANKANNI RAJ

Former Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president K. Selvaperunthagai and State Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan engaged in a war of words after the former said the law and order situation in Tamil Nadu was not satisfactory and the present scenario showed “films and real life” were vastly different from each other.

Speaking to the reporters on Saturday, he said: “The six months of the TVK-led government is a prime example that the dialogues spoken by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and his action in his movies cannot be realised in reality. They need to find the missing girl in Gingee. Action should be taken in the incidents that took place on Deepavali.”
Mr. Selvaperunthagai said: “To whom can the Collector go and complain? The State government should come out with a White Paper on the issue related to the Kallakurichi Collector and TVK MLA.”
In response, Mr. Viswanathan on Sunday said: “I don’t know which party Selvaperunthagai is in. I also don’t know which party he is going to go (next). Let him state that. I will answer after that.”

articles.title: Congress leader urges Amit Shah to address concerns of BCs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A.P. Congress Committee vice-president and A.P. Backward Classes Welfare Association convenor Kolanukonda Shivaji has written to Union Home Minister Amit Shah seeking his attention to the long-pending issues concerning the social, economic, educational and political empowerment of Backward Classes across the country.

Anticipating Mr. Amit Shah’s visit to Vijayawada on Monday, the Congress leader wrote the letter stating that BC communities continue to face inadequate representation and social inequalities, despite their contribution to nation building.

Ensuring their rightful share in governance and development is a constitutional obligation and a matter of social justice, he said, while placing a few demands including caste census; political reservation; provision of adequate reservation for BCs in State Legislative Assemblies and Parliament in proportion to their population; a dedicated BC sub quota in women’s reservation; separate Ministry for Backward Classes in the Union government; removal of 50% reservation limit to ensure proportionate representation for BCs in government employment, Parliament, State Legislatures and local self-governments.

These are not concessions or favours sought from the government, but legitimate constitutional rights and long-standing demands of BC communities, he said, urging Mr. Amit Shah to initiate appropriate legislative and administrative measures to fulfil the demands and uphold the principles of equality.

articles.title: 200 patients receive medical services at health camp
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Around 200 patients received medical services at a camp organised by Praja Arogya Vedika (PAV) and Jana Vignana Vedika in Vijayawada on Sunday.

The camp provided medical services, including consultations, medicines, guidance to patients suffering from diabetes, hypertension, epilepsy and paralysis at a minimal consultation fee. Later, volunteers distributed the required tablets and insulin to the patients and explained how to take the medicine.
PAV NTR district general secretary G. Vijay Prakash said such camps were being held once every two months for the benefit of the public, and the next one will be held on January 17.
A medical team from HCG Cancer Hospital also conducted free cancer screening tests for patients at the camp.

articles.title: Nearly 2,200 migrants reach Canary Islands in two days, Spain says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Spain declared a migration emergency on the islands on November 11 following a rise in arrivals in recent weeks, particularly from sub-Saharan Africa
Nearly 2,200 migrants have reached Spain's Canary Islands by boat over the past two days, Spain's maritime rescue service said on Sunday.

The archipelago off northwest Africa is a major entry point for migrants, mainly from West Africa, attempting the dangerous Atlantic crossing in makeshift boats. More than 13,000 of the just over 28,000 people who arrived in Spain by sea between January and the end of October landed in the Canary Islands, according to the Interior Ministry.

Spain declared a migration emergency on the islands on Tuesday (November 11, 2026) following a rise in arrivals in recent weeks, particularly from sub-Saharan Africa. The country is due to hold an early general election in two weeks.

articles.title: Southeast Asian leaders denounce violence in Myanmar, extend ban on its leader
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: ASEAN leaders proposed the plan in April 2021 to try to ease the violence that erupted after the army seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi

Southeast Asian leaders said on Sunday (November 15, 2026) that Myanmar has failed to comply with a 2021 peace plan and that its military and other armed groups continue to attack civilians, prompting them to extend a ban on Myanmar's leader attending the bloc's annual summits.

The stern rebuke by leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, who opened their annual summit meetings in the Philippine capital on Sunday (November 14, 2026), came during a review of the progress on the five-point peace plan by the country's military-backed government. Myanmar is a member of the 11-nation regional bloc.

ASEAN leaders proposed the plan in April 2021 to try to ease the violence that erupted after the army seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi. The army's takeover triggered widespread pro-democracy protests that were brutally quashed, leading to armed resistance and a civil war that has spread over much of the country.

The leaders reiterated “deep concern” over insufficient progress in implementing the peace plan. They urged all parties and stakeholders in Myanmar, "in particular the armed forces, security forces and armed groups to de-escalate violence and stop targeted attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure and enhance trust-building efforts.”
Last month, a United Nations rights investigator said the military-backed government in Myanmar was intentionally attacking civilians to terrorise them and force them into submission.

The leaders said the ban on Myanmar's leader and foreign minister attending ASEAN summit meetings would continue “until there is meaningful progress in the implementation” of the peace plan. The plan calls, among others, for an immediate end to hostilities and the start of dialogue mediated by the regional bloc's special envoy.

Under the ban, Myanmar can be represented only by lower-level career diplomats, including at the ongoing ASEAN meetings in Manila. Myanmar was due to hold ASEAN's rotating chair this year and host its multiple regional meetings, but because of the civil strife, the role passed to the Philippines.

“There's still certain bombings and displacement of Myanmar people, so step-by-step, we give it to them, how they're going to tackle this issue, and we'll monitor that,” Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro, ASEAN's current special envoy to Myanmar, said in a news conference in Manila.

The three-day summit, which includes scheduled talks with world leaders led by U.S. President Donald Trump, will focus on conflicts, including the war in Myanmar, according to drafts of post-summit communiques seen by The Associated Press .

articles.title: Taliban authorities ban cricket on Kandahar radio
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The government has shown support for the game, hosting cricket matches during the August anniversary of its return to power

The Taliban authorities have banned radio stations in southern Kandahar from airing content related to cricket, a rapidly growing sport in Afghanistan, two broadcasters and a provincial source told AFP on Sunday (November 15, 2026).
The government has shown support for the game, hosting cricket matches during the August anniversary of its return to power.
But the provincial Information and Culture Department told radio stations on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that anything related to cricket is no longer allowed.
A source from that department, who requested anonymity because he was not authorised to speak to the media, confirmed that “cricket coverage is banned”.
“Both commentary and news coverage, or even reporting about their winning result, is also banned,” he told AFP , without providing further details.
The head of a local radio station told AFP : “We received a call from Information and Culture, and we were told that we can’t cover cricket on the radio anymore.”
The manager of another Kandahar radio station confirmed the directive, saying that the authorities called and said “anything related to cricket is banned for now”.
Both broadcasters spoke to AFP on condition of anonymity for security reasons.
Afghanistan’s cricket board did not respond immediately to an AFP request for comment on the decision in Kandahar, which is home to the country’s supreme leader.
The Taliban authorities have restricted some sports in Afghanistan — outlawing mixed martial arts — but have allowed men and boys to continue playing cricket.
Women and girls, however, are banned from gyms and sports more broadly as part of rules severely limiting their access to public life.
The men’s cricket team is currently playing the second Test against Zimbabwe in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates.

articles.title: Respiratory illnesses rise in Gaza with worst to come as winter floods arrive, WHO says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Respiratory infections currently make up 11% of all consultations, with the WHO ‌expecting cold weather, flooding, overcrowded shelters and poor ventilation to push these numbers higher

​The World Health Organisation warned on Friday (November 13, 2026) of surging respiratory illnesses in Gaza, with worse expected after ‌heavy rains flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced Palestinians.

“The numbers ​already show the pressure. Acute respiratory infections are 33,000 cases higher than at ⁠the same time last year,” Dr. Reinhilde Van De Weerdt, WHO representative in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, told reporters in Geneva from Jerusalem.

Poor living conditions and severe overcrowding are driving up infections as Gaza’s population ‌is squeezed into an ever-smaller area, WHO said. The crunch has worsened as the Israeli military expands its control by advancing the “Yellow Line” — a demarcation established under ‌October’s U.S.-brokered ceasefire.
“That means people are living in more crowded conditions, where of course ‌the ⁠spread between humans of a virus is much more prone to spread,” Ms. Van ⁠De Weerdt explained.

The Israeli military told Reuters the Yellow Line aims to protect Israeli civilians and army troops from threats and that adjustments to its location follow the ceasefire agreement and international law, and are not intended ​to harm the civilian population.
“The IDF categorically ‌rejects the claim that it operates to deliberately reduce the area available to the civilian population in the Gaza Strip.”

COGAT, the Israeli military agency that coordinates aid, said that more than 93,000 tents and over 8,600 trucks carrying tarpaulin sheets, blankets and winter clothing ‌have entered Gaza since the Board of Peace, UN agencies and NGOs launched ​the winterisation plan. Equipment intended for the reconstruction of Gaza will be permitted to enter only after Hamas has been fully disarmed, it added.
Last week ⁠COGAT said that it had stepped up efforts to improve sanitary conditions before the heavy rain, in coordination with international organisations.
Respiratory infections currently make up 11% of all consultations, with the WHO ‌expecting cold weather, flooding, overcrowded shelters and poor ventilation to push these numbers higher.
“It is shocking that just a few days of rain really showed us what the coming months will bring. And winter has not even fully set in. The worst really is yet to come,” Ms. Van De Weerdt said.
Nearly a million displaced people in Gaza live in flood-exposed areas, and 400,000 of them are in locations that are considered at extremely high risk, according to ‌the WHO.

The agency said flooding heightened the risk of contaminated water, while standing water gave mosquitoes and ​pests more places to breed. Dampness encouraged mould and bacteria that are major drivers of respiratory infections, especially in young children, it said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The agency said flooding heightened the risk of contaminated water, while standing water gave mosquitoes and ​pests more places to breed. Dampness encouraged mould and bacteria that are major drivers of respiratory infections, especially in young children, it said.

articles.title: Drone ownership ban comes into force in Beijing over security concerns
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The ban applies to both urbanised and rural areas in the municipality of around 16,400 square kilometres (6,300 square miles) — an area roughly half the size of Belgium
Beijing’s ban on possessing drones came into force on Sunday (November 15, 2026), a measure authorities said will help ensure the security of China’s capital city.
The ban applies to both urbanised and rural areas in the municipality of around 16,400 square kilometres (6,300 square miles) — an area roughly half the size of Belgium.
The ban, which Beijing announced in September, outlaws owning and storing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to “safeguard the security of the capital”.
Transporting drones or their components into the city was also forbidden.
Owners had been forced to get rid of their devices ahead of Sunday’s (November 15, 2026) implementation, either by reselling them at approved buy-back points or online.
They could also have transported them outside the enforcement area.
Beijing, home to China’s central government, top leaders and the headquarters of the ruling Chinese Communist Party (CCP), has faced strict security measures.
The ban comes after airspace safety fears were raised in June when a small plane crashed into the city’s tallest skyscraper, killing the pilot and injuring 13 others.
Beijing had already banned drone sales in May 2026, with owners required to register their devices with authorities but permitted to keep them.
Now, anyone in possession of a drone could face a fine and the confiscation of their equipment.
Exemptions for drone flights may be granted for specific reasons such as counterterrorism, law enforcement, emergency relief, agriculture or scientific research.
Drones have become extremely popular in China in recent years, particularly for filming landscapes.

The announcement signalled the apparent ‌end of a six-week government counteroffensive to reclaim the coast near the mouth of the ​Red Sea, seized by the Houthis in September in a lightning advance that ⁠squeezed oil exports.

Sunday's announcement of a government retreat raises the prospect of new Houthi advances towards Aden, and underscores the predicament faced by Saudi Arabia in trying to stop the Houthis' drone and missile attacks on the kingdom. The government ‌forces have been based in Aden on the southern coast since 2015 after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa.

Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and ‌Red Sea shipping in recent months have strengthened the position of Iran in the wider West Asia conflict ⁠launched by the United States and Israel in February.

"The Southern Armed Forces announce the ⁠implementation of a redeployment operation for its forces from Dhubab Airport and the Bab el-Mandeb area, west of Taiz Governorate," the main military force fighting for Yemen's government in the south of the country said in a statement.
"This step is taken based ​on the priority of securing the capital, Aden, ‌and the neighbouring governorates, as well as strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats."
There was no immediate response from the Houthis, or from Saudi Arabia, the Yemeni government's main international ally.

Yemen's decade-long civil war, which had been dormant since 2022, abruptly reignited this summer as a ‌spillover from the Iran conflict. The Houthis made rapid gains to capture the coast along the ​Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which controls access to it, while besieging government forces in Taiz, the country's third-biggest city, in mountains above the approach to Aden.

A ⁠Saudi-backed government offensive last month rapidly retook key positions around the strait, notably Dhubab, but failed to drive the Houthis entirely away from the area or to retake the city of al-Mocha further up the coast.

The ‌Houthis have responded by intensifying drone and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia, grounding flights with strikes on its main airports as well as setting global energy markets on edge by targeting energy facilities.

They also made significant advances in the highland areas north of Aden, cutting off Taiz in early October and putting increased pressure on the disparate coalition of forces fighting for the internationally recognised government.

Around Bab el-Mandeb the government forces have redeployed to al-Suqyah, just south of ‌Dhubab and 150 km (95 miles) west of Aden, but are still trying to push the Houthis from coastal areas nearby, Yemeni ​military sources said.

articles.title: Czechs gather in big numbers to reject government's plan to overhaul funding of public media
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The massive protest took place at the capital's Letná Park, where huge crowds gathered during the 1989 Velvet Revolution, which ended more than 40 years of communist rule in the country

Hundreds of thousands of people rallied in Prague on Sunday (November 15, 2026) against a plan by the government of Czech billionaire Andrej Babis to overhaul funding for public broadcasters that many say will erode media independence and democracy.
The massive protest took place at the capital's Letná Park, where huge crowds gathered during the 1989 Velvet Revolution, which ended more than 40 years of communist rule in the country.

The rally, just two days before the anniversary of the 1989 protests, drew an estimated 350,000 people, said Mikulas Minar, the lead organizer from the Million Moments for Democracy group. They demanded that the government withdraw its plan and expressed concern that Babis and his coalition partners pose a threat to democracy.
“We do witness here something extraordinary today,” Mr. Minar said.

Under the plan, the country's public radio and television broadcasters would be financed from the state budget, replacing the existing system of regular fees paid by individuals, households and businesses. The broadcasters would receive about 15% less money than they do now, which could lead to layoffs, limited production and program cancellations.

Critics say the overhaul would give the three-party coalition the means to take control of the media, similar to what populist governments did in Slovakia under Prime Minister Robert Fico and in Hungary, before former Prime Minister Viktor Orban was ousted from power in April.
“We refuse the Slovak scenario,” one protest banner read. “Hands off the media,” said another.

The ruling coalition unexpectedly moved ahead with the plan in the lower house of Parliament on Oct. 24. Its lawmakers limited the opposition's speaking time before voting at 4.36 a.m. to advance the bill through the first of three parliamentary readings.

Thousands took to the streets the following day to protest the rushed process, and public media employees went on strike on Nov. 3. The strike was backed by labor unions, universities, students, churches, artists, athletes and international media organizations, among others.
“We are here to stand up against the rule by force in the style of 4:36,” Mr. Minár said Sunday (November 15, 2026), referring to the time the bill cleared its first reading.

Media freedom and the rule of law in the Czech Republic were debated Wednesday in the European Parliament. EU Justice Commissioner Michael McGrath said national legislation must ensure that funding for public service iis based on transparent and objective criteria and guarantees "adequate, sustainable and predictable financial resources.”
Mr. Babiš vowed to press ahead with the plan despite the protests and denied that it would affect media freedom.

articles.title: Mumbai to host sixth Earthshot Prize Awards on November 17; organisers promise biggest edition yet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Mumbai will host the sixth annual Earthshot Prize Awards on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), with Prince William and Catherine, Princess of Wales, attending the ceremony that will recognise five winners from among 15 finalists developing solutions to some of the world’s most pressing environmental challenges. The event will be part of a series of programmes organised during Earthshot Week, including the first-ever Children’s Earthshot Awards and an international gathering of environmental innovators, investors and business leaders.

The royal couple will arrive in Mumbai on Monday (November 16, 2026), marking their first visit to India together since 2016. They are also scheduled to participate in a game of gully cricket alongside young people from communities across Mumbai at Ballard Estate.
Speaking at a media briefing in Mumbai on Sunday (November 15, 2026), a Kensington Palace spokesperson said the Prince and Princess were looking forward to returning to India after a decade.

“The Prince is hugely excited to be here. For him, Earthshot has always been about urgent optimism—not simply talking about the environmental challenges facing our planet, but identifying the people who are solving them and helping those solutions reach more people more quickly,” the spokesperson said.
ALSO WATCH Watch: An exclusive conversation with Earthshot Prize CEO Jason Knauf | Pulse Maharashtra

The spokesperson said India had produced more Earthshot Prize winners and finalists than any other country, making it a fitting destination for what organisers described as their largest Earthshot programme yet.

The Earthshot Prize, founded by Prince William in 2020, identifies and supports environmental solutions across five categories. Each of the five winners will receive £1 million to help scale their innovations.

The awards ceremony on Tuesday will feature appearances and performances by several Indian and international celebrities, including Sachin Tendulkar, Alia Bhatt, Shreya Ghoshal, Rami Malek and British pop group Take That.

The ceremony will also feature the first Earthshot Orchestra, with Mumbai-based all-female hip-hop collective Wild Wild Women performing a version of The Chemical Brothers’ Galvanize . Take That will perform their new song Higher ,alongside one of their popular hits, while Indian composer Shashwat Sachdev will close the show.
For the first time, the ceremony will be streamed through Prime Video in more than 240 countries and territories, organisers said.

The Earthshot Prize’s Executive Director of Communications said the organisation had considered nearly 7,000 nominations from 169 countries since 2020. This year’s finalists represent a range of approaches, from community-led environmental initiatives to artificial intelligence-based climate technologies.
For the first time, major corporations are among the finalists, including India’s Mahindra Last Mile Mobility and Denmark’s Ørsted.

articles.title: Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries

On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.

India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

articles.keyPoints:
• India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries
• On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.
• India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

articles.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A 54-year-old man was arrested by the Veppankuppam police on charges of setting on fire his daughter’s house at Agaram village near Odugathur town at foothills of Jawadhu Hills in Vellore on Friday.

Police said the accused R. Anandan, 54, a wage labourer, was upset over his daughter Vaishnavi marrying Rajesh, a milk van driver, against his wishes. In a fit of rage, Anandan allegedly set on fire Rajesh’s father Kumar’s house in Agaram village. Residents alerted Veppankuppam police, who rushed to the spot with firefighters. articles.title: Tamil Nadu engages realty developers to fast track Global Capability Centre corridors
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: To advance the implementation of the Tamil Nadu GCC Corridor and Development Programme, the Department of Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce, Government of Tamil Nadu, convened a roundtable discussion at Guidance Tamil Nadu on Friday with leading real estate developers from Tamil Nadu and across the country, in the presence of Industries Minister S. Keerthana.

According to details shared by Guidance, the discussion focused on accelerating the development of Grade-A office space and supporting infrastructure across the identified corridors to meet the needs of the state’s growing Global Capability Centre (GCC) ecosystem. The roundtable brought together developers’ perspectives on strengthening these corridors as integrated destinations for GCC investment and growth.

Tamil Nadu is home to more than 460 GCCs, including over 405 in Chennai, with the sector adding more than 55,000 jobs in 2025. Continued expansion by existing centres, alongside interest from new investors, has increased the need for readily available, high-quality office space.

Participants discussed measures to accelerate project development, maintain competitive rentals and ensure that suitable space is available within the timelines required by global companies. Developers shared their perspectives on land availability, development costs, floor space index (FSI), approval processes and infrastructure requirements.

The discussion emphasised the importance of developing complete GCC ecosystems in Rajiv Gandhi Salai (OMR), Pallavaram–Thoraipakkam Radial Road (PTR) and Mount–Poonamallee High Road (MPR) through mixed-use projects that integrate offices with housing, schools, healthcare, hospitality and retail. Public transport, last-mile connectivity and pedestrian access were identified as essential to supporting the growth of these corridors. Participants noted and appreciated the greater transparency and accountability they had experienced in their interactions with government departments, with fewer discretionary hurdles contributing to a more conducive environment for investment.
The roundtable also provided an opportunity to encourage greater use of the State’s Single Window Portal and explore investments beyond Chennai, including in emerging locations such as Hosur.

articles.title: BIM, Texas university to offer course on AI in Business from next year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Bharathidasan Institute of Management (BIM), in collaboration with the University of Texas at Arlington (UTA) in the U.S., on Friday announced the launch of the Master of Science programme in Artificial Intelligence for Business (MSAIB), which is aimed at working professionals in India.

On Friday, representatives of the two institutions exchanged Memoranda of Understanding for the course. The first batch of the course will start in August 2027. The first cohort will include 25 students, mostly working professionals, who are keen to upgrade their skills to secure better job opportunities in multinational companies, and the tuition fee is indicated to be around $27,000.

Asit K. Barma, Director, BIM, told presspersons in Chennai that the classes would be held at the IIT-Madras Research Park. The location, being a technology hub, will be beneficial to students in terms of access to industry interactions.

The conventional MBA course had, over the past few years, been losing its shine gradually, indicated by the falling enrolment for the Common Admission Test (CAT). Last year, there was a 2% drop in students taking the Common Admission Test compared to the previous year, Dr. Barma said. The two-year MSAIB course will provide an opening for young professionals to pursue an industry-oriented course, he said.
Fernando Jaramillo, Associate Dean, College of Business, UTA, said the course would be offered in hybrid mode, with faculty members from the UTA visiting the Chennai campus for conducting classes.
The curriculum for the course would be the same as the one offered at its Arlington campus.

Radha K. Mahapatra, Chair and Professor, Information Systems and Operations Management, UTA, said the faculty for each course would spend about a week on the Chennai campus, while the rest of the classes would be conducted online. For the intake of students, candidates’ holistic performance, including undergraduate GPA score, rigour of courses taken, exposure to mathematics, and even job experience, will be considered, UTA representatives said.

Ravi Appaswamy, chairman, Board of Governors, BIM, said the MSAIB course would provide an avenue for young professionals to learn the use of a tool that had become so indispensable to every profession and industry.
R. Siddharthan, managing director, Accenture India, and Mafruza Sultana, assistant professor and faculty chair-international relations, BIM, were among those present.

articles.title: Over 7,000 books removed from District Central Libraries in Vellore, nearby districts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ranipet and Tirupattur have the highest number (2,401) of books each from these publications

As many as 7,995 books published by the controversial Agalvilakku and Phoenix Publications were removed from the racks of District Central Library in Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur, and Tiruvannamalai districts on Friday.

The action comes against the backdrop of allegations of fake and AI-generated books being procured from these publishers for public libraries including Periyar Arivulagam, a newly inaugurated public library in Coimbatore. “The identified books of the two publications were removed from the other books. The books, which are meant for distribution to branch libraries in the district for 2025-26, are stored in a separate room,” S. Valli, District Library Officer (Tiruvannamalai), told The Hindu.

Ranipet and Tirupattur have the highest number (2,401) of books each from these publications, followed by Tiruvannamalai (2,209 books), and Vellore (984 books). “Books on competitive examinations are a big attraction in District Central library as the facility has a large collection of books related to general knowledge,” said G. Satish, a reader.

Officials said District Central Library in these districts have books on subjects including history, politics, law, economics, philosophy, agriculture, computer and mathematics. Reference books, especially for examinations conducted by the Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission (TNPSC), UPSC, and other competitive exams are available.

As per norms, around 60,000 to 70,000 books are procured for each district library annually based on feedback provided by local librarians and readers. These books then distributed branch libraries in the district. As per estimates, Vellore and Tiruvannamalai have at least 120 branch libraries each whereas Ranipet and Tirupattur have around 50 branch libraries each.

articles.title: Turkiye, Qatar sign mutual defence agreement, Turkish presidency says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Turkiye and Qatar were working to develop and diversify their energy partnership, and that their cooperation ‌in the defence industry would ​continue to grow, a statement from the Turkish presidency quoted President Erdogan as saying

Turkiye and ​Qatar signed a mutual defence agreement on Friday (November 13, 2026), ‌the office of President Tayyip Erdogan said, ​as the Turkish leader ⁠met the Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al-Thani in Istanbul.

“President Erdogan stated that we ‌would continue working together to prevent the resurgence of war in ‌the Gulf region and establish a ‌basis ⁠for dialogue and achieve peace,” ⁠the presidency said in a statement on X, which did not provide details on the defence accord.
The ​statement cited ‌him as saying that Turkiye and Qatar were working to develop and diversify their energy partnership, and that their cooperation ‌in the defence industry would ​continue to grow.
“President Erdogan stated that the Mutual Defence Agreement signed today ⁠by Turkey and Qatar would add another dimension to our brotherhood,” it added.
In August, ‌Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement in Mecca, bringing together the Sunni Muslim U.S. allies at a time of conflict across the region.

Turkiye’s parliament ratified the ‌so-called Mecca Joint Defence Agreement last week, clearing ​the way for Ankara to send military support to Saudi Arabia, which ⁠has been struggling to fend off attacks ⁠by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi militants.
Under the agreement, signed by the three ‌regional powers in August, an attack on one party constitutes an attack ​on all.

articles.title: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security

Urgent pleas for cash from poor ​nations most exposed to the kind of climate-related disasters that have marked this year risk meeting a sluggish response at Turkiye’s COP31 talks as Western governments put ‌national security and living costs first.

Two years ago, rich countries agreed at UN climate talks they would triple ​climate funding for poorer countries to $300 billion per year by 2035 versus a previous 2020 target. Also by 2035, financing ⁠from all public and private sources combined would be $1.3 trillion annually.
The rich countries met their 2020 target two years late.

Since then, climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security.
Vulnerable small island nations say the cash they need to repair damage and to guard against future climate-related crises is again arriving too slowly and their own budgets have shrunk.

“Like many small island ‌developing states, we remain in a perpetual climate disaster recovery mode,” Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale told the conference. “We cannot build resilience ‌while ⁠our fiscal space erodes.”
Even when money is available, technical hurdles set by lenders can stretch the administrative capacity of ⁠small states.
For many developed nations, facing international and domestic unrest as citizens protest against the rising cost of living, their focus has narrowed.

Britain, which has sought to be a leader in addressing climate change, said in July savings made from switching some climate finance contributions from grants to loans would be used to help fund a cap on ​domestic bus fares.
The Stockholm ‌International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) estimated in April that world military expenditure reached $2.89 trillion in 2025, up 2.9% in real terms from 2024.
Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine said military defence ultimately was the smaller concern.

“We are told there is no money, but as spending on war grows, the greatest security threat we face remains underfunded. I appeal to you: Find money for life, not death,” she said ‌in her speech to the conference in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

articles.title: Microsoft outage hits businesses worldwide; India feels impact
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Disruption to Microsoft’s cloud-based email service affects business operations and airline customer support in India; public services in several countries also report problems

The global disruption of multiple Microsoft services, which began on Thursday (November 12, 2026) and continued late into Friday (November 13, 2026), affected several Indian businesses’ internal communications and customer-facing operations.

In its latest update on Friday (November 13, 2026), the company said it was making progress in fixing the outage, which has affected email access and workplace applications in businesses, public services, and other organisations across the globe. In India, the disruptions affected businesses from startups to multinational corporations.

A senior executive at a major telecom company in India told The Hindu that employees were unable to access emails or send service-disruption alerts to customers. Call-centre traffic also increased, the executive said.

Rahul Ganapathy, co-founder and CEO of deep tech startup Atsuya Technologies, said customer emails and scheduled Teams meetings were disrupted, although his company did not rely entirely on Microsoft internally.
At a Big Four professional services firm in Bengaluru, a senior employee said its internal operations were affected, but added that IT teams were restoring services.
The disruptions also left airlines experiencing customer-support delays.

IndiGo said its email support was affected and advised customers to use 6E Skai, its AI-powered virtual assistant. Akasa Air warned of email support delays and directed passengers to its customer care centre and social media. Air India said flight operations were unaffected, although it rerouted emails.

Separately, India’s Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, issued a high-severity advisory on Friday, warning of multiple vulnerabilities in Microsoft products. It flagged an Outlook vulnerability that it said was being actively exploited and urged users to apply security updates. The advisory did not explicitly link the vulnerabilities to the outage.

Microsoft identified Exchange Online — described as its cloud-based messaging platform that delivers email, calendar, contacts, and tasks — as the primary service affected. Some Microsoft Graph requests accessing Exchange Online data timed out, affecting dependent features in Teams, Copilot, and SharePoint, the company said. Core Teams messaging and online meetings largely continued normally, it added.

On Friday, Microsoft said recovery was progressing, with improvements in North America and Europe and encouraging signs in Asia-Pacific. Service availability and email delivery were improving, but intermittent access problems and delays could continue, it said, adding that it was working through email backlogs and retained a 48-hour timeout window to protect delayed messages. Service health and capacity had not fully returned to baseline, it said.

Around 8 p.m. IST on Friday (November 13, 2026), Charles Lamanna, executive vice president of Copilot, Agents and Platform at Microsoft, said, "We’re seeing encouraging recovery progress, with service availability and email delivery performance improving across a growing portion of affected infrastructure. We know our customers rely on our services to get important work done every day, and regret the impact these outages had on those who depend on us. Our teams are reviewing what happened and how we can prevent similar issues going forward."

The company said it was not aware of any malicious activity causing the disruption and promised that it would publish a detailed report on the root cause and corrective measures after services were restored.

articles.title: The challenge of holding the Quad together
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The big ticket question confronting the Quad, however, is how Donald Trump engages with the group and the broader Indo-Pacific geography

Speaking to the media on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta, the U.S. Secretary of State announced that the leaders of the four Quad countries — India, Australia, Japan and the U.S. — are expected to meet in Manila in November, on the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit. The announcement is significant, as this would be the first summit-level meeting of the Quad leaders since Donald Trump began his second term as U.S. President. It would also be the first such summit attended by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi since she assumed office. The last Quad Leaders’ Summit was held in Wilmington in 2024, when Joe Biden was U.S. President and Fumio Kishida was Japan’s Prime Minister.

While India was expected to host the subsequent Quad Leaders’ Summit, the grouping underwent a period of intense strategic turbulence in 2025, on account of Washington’s shifting geopolitical priorities and changing political dynamics in its bilateral relations with Quad members, especially India. However, this did not result in complete collapse of the grouping. Apart from the leader-level summit, the group has remained successful in continuing its operational synergies in its various initiatives. This was most evident in the elevation of the Quad’s Indo-Pacific Maritime Domain Awareness initiative to the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration framework, launched in New Delhi in May 2026, following the Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting.
National & Polity Report: The challenge of holding the Quad together. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and administrative governance framework.

Institutional Framework: The update directly connects with parliamentary procedures, centre-state relations under the Seventh Schedule, and constitutional bodies responsible for upholding statutory mandates.
